```{r}
#| label: setup-idalia
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# Load hourly KTPA observations
event_data <- read_csv("data/ktpa_2023.csv", col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(grepl(":53:", DATE)) |>
  mutate(
    datetime = as.POSIXct(DATE),
    temp = parse_number(HourlyDryBulbTemperature),
    pressure = parse_number(HourlyStationPressure),
    wind = parse_number(HourlyWindSpeed),
    precip = replace_na(parse_number(na_if(HourlyPrecipitation, "T")), 0)
  ) |>
  filter(datetime >= as.POSIXct("2023-08-28 00:00:00") & datetime <= as.POSIXct("2023-08-31 23:59:59"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-telemetry-idalia
#| fig-cap: "Hourly meteorological telemetry recorded at Tampa International Airport (KTPA) during the event window. Top: Barometric pressure (inHg). Bottom: Sustained wind speed (mph)."
#| fig-width: 9.5
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| dpi: 180

# Panel 1: Barometric Pressure
p1 <- ggplot(event_data, aes(x = datetime, y = pressure)) +
  geom_line(color = "#047857", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(data = filter(event_data, pressure == min(pressure, na.rm = TRUE)), color = "#dc2626", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Hurricane Idalia (2023): KTPA Telemetry Breakdown",
    subtitle = "Station Pressure (inHg) & Sustained Wind Speed (mph)",
    y = "Pressure (inHg)",
    x = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, color = "#0f172a"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#475569", size = 10, margin = margin(b = 8)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#047857", size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# Panel 2: Wind Speed
p2 <- ggplot(event_data, aes(x = datetime, y = wind)) +
  geom_line(color = "#059669", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(data = filter(event_data, wind == max(wind, na.rm = TRUE)), color = "#dc2626", size = 3) +
  labs(
    y = "Wind Speed (mph)",
    x = "Date & Time (EDT)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#0f172a", margin = margin(t = 6)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#059669", size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

p1 / p2
```


## Synoptic Evolution & Gulf Acceleration

In late August 2023, Hurricane Idalia rapidly intensified over exceptionally warm eastern Gulf waters, ballooning into a Category 4 major hurricane before making landfall in Florida's Big Bend as a Category 3 storm on August 30.

Although Idalia tracked roughly 120 miles west of Tampa Bay, its eastern flank unleashed persistent southerly and southwesterly gales that pushed Gulf water directly into the mouth of Tampa Bay. Crucially, the surge arrived precisely during an astronomical **King Tide** (supermoon peak).

## Meteorological Telemetry at KTPA

KTPA's telemetry documented the dynamics of a high-tide surge disaster:

- **Pressure & Wind Signature:** Station pressure fell to **29.55 inHg** on August 30, with sustained onshore winds of **33 mph** and squall gusts over 50 mph driving ocean water inland.
- **Unprecedented Coastal Inundation:** The combined astronomical King Tide and 4 to 5 foot surge pushed Tampa Bay to its highest water level since 1993 at the time. Water completely submerged Bayshore Boulevard, flowed through ground-floor condominiums on Davis Islands, and cut off access to Gulf beach communities in St. Petersburg and Clearwater.
- **Rainfall Total:** Outer bands dropped **2.68 inches of rain** at KTPA, while the primary damage was caused by saltwater flooding.


## Hurricane Idalia Landfall: Shape, Rotation & Wind Circulation

The interactive simulation below reconstructs Hurricane Idalia at mainland Florida landfall near Keaton Beach (Cat 3, 125 mph). It visualizes the storm's cyclonic rainbands, counter-clockwise rotation, and the resulting onshore southwesterly winds that triggered historic high-tide coastal surge across Bayshore Boulevard.
